metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent high for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often lags; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (especially in first 5–7 days of forecast horizon), model exhibits “overconfident” bias; reduce early forecast by 3–7%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to over-smooth; add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
